By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
filed by the petitioner Nirmala with respect to the injuries caused to her in a motor vehicle accident.

The accident in the present case took place on 07.08.2017, at around 06:45 AM.
The petitioner Nirmala and her husband Inder Bhushan Sharma were going to their village from Sikarpur on their motorcycle registration No. DL-UP-14X 4437.

When they reached near Village Mirzapur,
Bulandshahar, a Wagon R car registration No. DL 7CE-9440, driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Bhagwat Singh Gautam, came from opposite side at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, and hit their motorcycle.
Due to this collision, she suffered multiple injuries all over her body and head injuries.
Her husband Inder Bhushan Sharma died on the spot.
She was taken to District Hospital, Bulandsharhar, where she was referred to Kailash Hospital Khurja.
Two claim petitions have been filed, one with respect to the death of Inder Bhushan Sharma and other with respect to injuries to the petitioner Nirmala.
By order dated 02.07.2019 both the cases were consolidated and the case related to the death of Inder Bhushan Sharma was treated as the main case and common evidence was recorded.
This case relates to the injuries of Nirmala.
According to the claim petition, she is a home maker.

She was immediately taken to District Hospital,
Bulandsharar, where she was referred to Kailash Hospital Khurja.
She remained hospitalised from 07.08.2017 to 14.08.2017.
According to the disability certificate, she is a case of Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others permanent disability to the extent of 32% cognitive dysfunction due to head injuries.

8. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1: Whether Smt. Nirmala sustained injuries in a motor vehicular accident on 07.08.2017 at about 6.45 a.m. near Village Mirzapur, Buland Shahar, U.P. within jurisdiction of PS Kotwali Dehat, Buland Shahar, U.P. due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing registration No.DL 7CE 9440 (WagonR) driven by the respondent No. 1 /Bhagwat Singh Gautam?(OPP)
9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.

sentences.text: 10. Now in this case, the petitioner Nirmala is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish her claim, she has examined herself as PW-1 and proved copy of her aadhar card, copy of driving licence of deceased Ex.PW1/5, medical bills Ex.PW1/7.
She stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
She has deposed that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent act of the respondent no. 1, who was the driver of the car.

She has deposed that on 07.08.2017, at about 06:30 AM in the morning, at around 06:45 AM she and her husband Inder Bhushan Sharma were going to their village from Sikarpur on their motorcycle registration No. DL- UP-14X 4437.

When they reached near Village Mirzapur, Bulandshahar, a Wagon R car registration No. DL 7CE-9440, driven by its driver respondent no.1 Bhagwat Singh Gautam, came from opposite side at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, and hit their motorcycle.
Due to this accident, her husband Inder Bhushan Sharma died on the spot.
She was immediately taken to District Hospital, Bulandsharar, where she was referred to Kailash Hospital Khurja where she remained hospitalised from 07.08.2017 to 14.08.2017.
According to the disability certificate, she is a case of permanent disability to the extent of 32% cognitive dysfunction due to head injuries.

11. The respondent no. 1 & 2 the driver and owner of the offending vehicle have not denied the accident or the involvement of their vehicle but has only said that the accident occurred due to the fault of the petitioner himself.

Although, they have averred about this defence Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others in their reply but have not proved anything in this regard nor led any evidence to prove anything contrary to claim of petitioner.

After investigation, the police filed the chargesheet against respondent no. 2 the driver of the car.
Filing of chargesheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima faice points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of chargesheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such chargesheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.

14. In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence, it is proved that Inder Bhushan Sharma died due to rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 Bhagwat Singh Gautam, the driver of Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others the offending car.

sentences.text: Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No. 2
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

16. In the case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, the Hon'ble Supreme Court while delineating on the general principles relating to compensation in injury cases observed that - "The provisions of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 ("the Act"), for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

entities.text: Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :

Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
Nirmala vs Bhagwat Singh Gautam (Driver) on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45899244/
4

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured , comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-pecuniary damages (General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

entities.text: Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under head (i), (ii) (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injuries, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the head (ii) (b),
(iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
Assessment of pecuniary damages under item (i) and (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of the actuals and are easily ascertainable from evidence.
Award under the head of future medical expenses - item (iii) depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for future treatment and cost thereof.

Assessment of non-pecuniary damages - item (iv), (v) and (vi)
involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury, deprivation, disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant.
Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others The Hon'ble Court further held that ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

entities.text: Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (a) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (b)
Nirmala vs Bhagwat Singh Gautam (Driver) on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45899244/
5

whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (c) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions,
but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.

If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others carpentry.

entities.text: Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of 'loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.

It may be noted that when compensation is awarded by treating the loss of future earning capacity as 100% (or even anything more than 50%), the need to award compensation separately under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others life may disappear and as a result, only a token or nominal amount may have to be awarded under the head of loss of amenities or loss of expectation of life, as otherwise there may be a duplication in the award of compensation.
17.

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation in this case is calculated as follows.

MEDICAL EXPENSES:
18.
Petitioner has proved the medical bills on record which are Ex.PW1/7.
However it is stated by the counsel for insurance company that the verified bills are of around Rs.91,361/-.
Counsel for petitioner has no objection if this amount is awarded as compensation.

Therefore, I award Rs.
91,361/- as medical expenses to the petitioner.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
19.
As per the affidavit of the petitioner, after the accident, she suffered permanent disability to the extent of 32% cognitive dysfunction due to head injuries.
Therefore considering this cognitive dysfunction disability and the inability of the petitioner to live a proper life due to it, I award Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT :

Petitioner has admitted that she is a home maker.
Therefore it is clear that she has no independent financial earnings.
However, record shows that she was hospitalised for around one and half months.
Therefore, the household work must have been done by some attendant.
Because she was not working at the time of accident, there Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others is no question of any compensation under this head.

sentences.text: The compensation under this head will be given and covered under attendant charges.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 21.
The petitioner has not separately proved any expenses in relation to conveyance, special diet or attendant charges.
But considering the situation of the petitioner, it is not difficult to understand that she must have incurred some money on these heads.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.10,000/- each to petitioner as conveyance and special diet charges.
22. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment and she has not claimed anything under this head.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
( DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- as attendant charges.

23. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.50,000/- (10,000+10,000+30,000)
under this head.

sentences.text: 24. The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability.
For this the income of the injured has to establish but because the petitioner is a home maker and has no fixed income or financial resources, her notional income has to be fixed for this purpose.

In Kirti and Another vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2021) 2 SCC 166), it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that one category of non earning victims that courts are often called upon to calculate the compensation for are home makers.

entities.text: Kirti and Another vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2021) 2 SCC 166)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A house maker often prepares food for the entire family, manages the procurement of groceries and other household shopping needs, cleans and manages the house and its surroundings, undertakes decoration, repairs and maintenance work, looks after the needs of the children and any aged member of the household,
manages budgets and so much more.

In rural households, they often also assist in the sowing,
harvesting and transplanting activities in the field, apart from tending cattle.

However, despite all the above, the conception that house makers do not "work" or that they do not add economic value to the household is a problematic idea that has persisted for many years and must be overcome.
The issue of fixing notional income for a home maker, therefore, serves extremely important functions.

Nirmala vs Bhagwat Singh Gautam (Driver) on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45899244/
7
It is a recognition of the multitude of women who are engaged in this activity, whether by choice or as a result of social/cultural norms.
It signals to society at large that the law and the courts of the land believe in the value of the labour, services and scarifies of homemakers.

It is an acceptance of the idea that these activities Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others contribute in a very real way to the economic condition of the family, and the economy of the nation, regardless of the fact that it may have been traditionally excluded from economic analyses it is a reflection of changing attitudes and mindsets and of our intentional law obligations.

entities.text: Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And, most importantly, it is step towards the constitutional vision of social equality and ensuring dignity of life to all individuals.
There can be no fixed approach to the issue of how such notional income of a homemaker is to be calculated.
It is to be understand that in such cases the attempt by the court is to fix an approximate economic value for all the work that a homemaker does, impossible though that task may be.
Courts must keep in mind the idea of awarding just compensation in such cases, looking to the facts and circumstances.
25. Therefore, one method to calculate the notional income of a housemaker can be the minimum wages.

In the present case also, it is expedient that the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.7400/- per month which were the minimum wages of unskilled workers in Uttar Pradesh on the date of accident (Manusha Sreekumar and Others vs United India Insurance Company Ltd. 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1441 and Kirti and Another vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2021) 2 SCC 166).

sentences.text: But considering the fact that the petitioner has 32% cognitive disability, it is not difficult to assume that this disability will definitely affect her day-to-day life and household work.
Therefore, I presume that she must have suffered at least 16% functional disability which is half of 32%, also in carrying on with her day to day activities and household work.

In view of this, I am of the opinion that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 16% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

The annual income of petitioner on the basis of minimum wages is Rs.88,800/-(7,400x12)
28.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
13. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of chargesheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.
If any party do not accept such chargesheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that chargesheet is collusive, it can record that chargesheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the chargesheet.
The court or the tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
Assessment of non-pecuniary damages - item (iv), (v) and (vi)
involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury, deprivation, disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant.
Therefore, the household work must have been done by some attendant.
It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.
For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
( DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
The issue of fixing notional income for a home maker, therefore, serves extremely important functions.
It is a recognition of the multitude of women who are engaged in this activity, whether by choice or as a result of social/cultural norms.
It is an acceptance of the idea that these activities Nirmala versus Bhagwat Singh Gautam & others contribute in a very real way to the economic condition of the family, and the economy of the nation, regardless of the fact that it may have been traditionally excluded from economic analyses it is a reflection of changing attitudes and mindsets and of our intentional law obligations.
And, most importantly, it is step towards the constitutional vision of social equality and ensuring dignity of life to all individuals.
There can be no fixed approach to the issue of how such notional income of a homemaker is to be calculated.
It is to be understand that in such cases the attempt by the court is to fix an approximate economic value for all the work that a homemaker does, impossible though that task may be.
Courts must keep in mind the idea of awarding just compensation in such cases, looking to the facts and circumstances.
25. Therefore, one method to calculate the notional income of a housemaker can be the minimum wages.
In the present case also, it is expedient that the notional income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.7400/- per month which were the minimum wages of unskilled workers in Uttar Pradesh on the date of accident (Manusha Sreekumar and Others vs United India Insurance Company Ltd. 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1441 and Kirti and Another vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited (2021) 2 SCC 166).
26.
In view of this, I am of the opinion that functional disability in relation to whole body of the petitioner must be considered as 16% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.
